title: Personal Credit Cards: When a Missed Autopay Debit Is the Bank's Error
content:
This page of the Personal Credit Cards manual states how a late payment fee on a card paid by automatic payment is found to be the bank's error, and what follows when it is not.

## Determination

A recent late payment fee still standing on the card is a fee the bank billed contrary to the card charter, to be taken back in full on the bank error ground, only when such a fee is present and each requirement this rule places on the automatic payment arrangement is satisfied: the instruction on the card, the checking account funding it, and the card's payment record for the due date. In that event the due-date debit of the automatic payment was one the bank failed to take, which makes the fee the bank's own error. Nothing is then drawn from the cardholder's courtesy allowance, and whether that allowance still has room makes no difference.

If no recent unreversed late payment fee is present, or if any single requirement on the arrangement fails, this rule supplies no ground of reversal at all. Whether the fee may instead come off as a courtesy is then decided solely on the general courtesy terms for late payment fees.

## Truth table

| Recent unreversed late fee present | Every requirement on the arrangement met | Ground under this rule | Courtesy allowance touched |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | bank error | no |
| yes | no, at least one fails | none | decided only under the general courtesy terms |
| no | any | none | not applicable |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical)

- A fee found to be the bank's error is reversed on that ground even if the cardholder has already used every courtesy reversal allowed on the tier, because the courtesy allowance is not consulted.
- A fee that fails one requirement is not partly the bank's error; the rule yields no ground, and the whole matter of a goodwill reversal rests on the courtesy terms.
